chunks: "I've used [tool(s) you've actually used, e. g. KiCad and Altium] . My main one is [tool] , which I used for [project: e. g. a four-layer STM32 motor controller board] .

I drew the schematic, made a few of my own symbols and footprints from the datasheet, ran ERC, laid out the board with controlled-impedance traces for USB, set up design rules to match the fabricator's capabilities, ran DRC, and generated Gerbers, drill files, the BOM and the pick-and-place file.

I know the others at a conceptual level and have looked at them: Eagle is simpler, with a single-file library model and ULPs for scripting; Altium has an integrated schematic-and-PCB environment with strong rules and collaboration; KiCad is open source and increasingly capable, with a Python API; and Allegro is the heavyweight in large companies, with a constraint manager and strong high-speed tools.
What I'd say is that the workflow is the same in all of them: library, schematic, ERC, netlist to layout, rules, DRC, outputs.
So if the team uses a tool I haven't, I'd expect to be productive in a week or two, mostly on library conventions and shortcuts.
I'd also learn the team's library and review processes first, because most layout errors start in the library."
